Current internal scene model:

View A: Attention is essentially fixed on the left location (selection probability 0.99995). That object is predicted yellow and triangular (color = yellow 1.0, shape = triangle 1.0) with high immediate access (recoverability now 0.846, then 0.672, 0.512). Other A locations are weakly attended: right is almost certainly red square (red 1.0, square 1.0) with tiny selection probability (0.00005) and lower recoverability (0.328 → 0.245 → 0.186); upper is very likely green circle; lower is very likely blue cross, both with near-zero current selection and lower recoverability.

Redirecting in A: issuing an “upper”, “right”, or “lower” command is predicted to move attention to that specified location (next-selection probabilities for those commands ≈0.997–0.999), so the system can shift selection away from the left.

View B: Attention is essentially fixed on the upper location (selection 0.99873). That object is predicted red and triangular (red ~0.9995, triangle ~0.9999) with modest recoverability (0.275 → 0.203 → 0.156). Other B locations are identifiable (right: yellow cross; lower: green circle; left: blue square) with near-zero current selection but higher recoverability for right (0.652 → 0.492 → 0.374).

Redirecting in B: “right”, “lower”, or “left” commands are predicted to move selection to those locations (each command yields ~0.999 probability of selecting its named location).
